newsitem.title: UK: Euro products outlook - gas oil set to slide.
newsitem.headline: Euro products outlook - gas oil set to slide.

text.p: Gas oil fundamentals look set to slide this week, but refiners may find comfort in tighter supplies of high octane gasoline which could brighten the picture.
"Gasoline has started to pick up the baton from distillates," said an oil trader at a major.
Refinery margins for fuel oil look to be pointing south, making extra supplies unlikely. Prices are set to drift sideways. Improved supplies of naphtha could soften the sector, traders said.
Increased supply and depressed demand for gas oil is likely to put further pressure on heating oil premiums this week.
Premiums for cargoes have come off about $5 in the past week and those for Russian are down about $2, pushed lower by the approach of U.S. cargoes.

"We are looking a bit weaker on physical for the next couple of weeks, but longer-term over the whole winter we could go back up because our stock-build remains below historical levels," said a trader. He saw heating oil premiums falling by $1-$2 over the week.
Bears see additional supply and demand that has been depressed by unseasonably mild weather in Germany, Europe's biggest heating oil market.

Low sulphur diesel premiums could be eroded as buyers continue to hold out for lower prices. Diesel premiums to November futures would fall by at least $10 per tonne to $18-$25, said one trader at a major.
In the Med, premiums may crumble because heating oil is well supplied and demand lacklustre.
Gasoline is set to be firm this week due to lower refinery production and further buying in the paper market ahead of the U.K. government's November budget, traders said.

High octane supplies have been tight recently due to poor reforming margins leading to throughtput cuts at several European refineries. But this margin has now recovered and could lead to better supplies towards the end of the month.
A continued shortage in the immediate term of high octane product was expected.
"I see the trend continuing next week and into November," said a trader. "Some refinery turnarounds in the Med have capped the number of cargoes available."

Naphtha was expected to ease slightly after Algeria's Skikda port reopened on Friday after closing on Tuesday morning due to bad weather. But one trader said the cargoes delayed by the closure all had been fixed to buyers, so there was no extra supply.

High sulphur cracked fuel oil is likely to gain support from Romanian demand and continuing poor refinery margins which point to no extra supplies of fuel. Prices look flat given no violent changes in crude.

Transatlantic interest may draw some material which could push prices slightly higher. "New York harbour prices are very strong and we could see fuel heading transatlantic. It's one to watch," said a trader at an oil major.

Enel's recent slow buying this year compared with last suggests to some dealers that the winter bounce may not be coming. "With more people using gas, is low sulphur going to be able to sustain its traditional premium?" asked one trader who saw prices holding around $135 cif Italy.
